articles.headline: Notes by the Way, No. II -- The Camp Meeting of Frederica Circuit, Delaware
articles.author: J. M. B.
articles.summary: For the Christian Recorder. A travel letter on the camp meeting at Felton (Frederica Circuit), Delaware, signed 'J. M. B.' dated Baltimore, August 27th, 1867. Names A.M.E. ministers born in Delaware (Anthony Campbell, James Towson, N. C. W. Cannon, Peter D. W. Schureman; of present ministers Bishop Campbell, M. M. Clark, H. J. Young, Geo. Boyer, R. P. Gibbs) and the camp-meeting preachers (Rev. R. Norris, Rev. Gilbert Waters, J. M. Brown, Bishop Wayman, Rev. Bro. Mason of the New England Conference, Rev. Bro. Bell, Rev. Richard Robinson lately returned from Hayti, Rev. Wm. W. Grimes, Rev. Geo. Boyer of Philadelphia, Rev. Bro. Polson of Wilmington, Rev. Bro. Davis (white), Brother David Lewis brother of Rev. Henry B. Lewis, Rev. Bro. Lofor of New Jersey, Rev. H. M. Lewis).
people: minister, of Philadelphia; preached at the camp meeting (Rev.)

articles.headline: Things in Philadelphia (editorial)
articles.summary: The people generally are well and active, now that the extra warm weather is about over. Nearly all have returned from the several watering places and country residences. The churches presented a very slim appearance last Sabbath on account of the camp-meetings. Rev. Theodore Gould is pushing ahead with his mission, and we hope the brethren will receive him with open hearts.
people: minister pushing his mission in Philadelphia (Rev.)

articles.headline: Quick Time (editorial account of the Turpin-Murrey wedding)
articles.summary: The editor records a quick trip to and from the wedding of Rev. J. P. Turpin and Miss Murrey of Brooklyn, L.I. Left Philadelphia Tuesday morning, Sept. 3d, at half-past 4 o'clock, accompanied by 'our good brother, Mr. Jones, and wife, and Miss Smith, all of whom reside in Addison street.' Took cars at foot of Walnut street by the Amboy Road; crossed to Brooklyn; the couple were married at about half-past two o'clock in Bridge street A. M. E. church by Rev. Bishop A. W. Wayman; reception at N. H. Lewis' residence in Carroll street, Brooklyn (Rev. N. H. Turpin, father of the groom). Returned to residence in Philadelphia at 10.25 P.M.
people: Bishop who performed the marriage (Rev., Bishop)

articles.headline: Letter from H. J. Rhodes
articles.author: H. J. Rhodes
articles.summary: For the Christian Recorder. A fund-raising travel letter dated Aug. 19th, 1867. Rhodes took the steamer John A. Warner on Aug. 4th 1867, landing at Bristol, Pa., met by Rev. B. Lewis; went to Bensalem; was collecting money to assist in building a church in West Philadelphia, Pa. Describes further travel to New York, Weeksville (Brooklyn) with Mr. J. Dickerson, Bethel church (Sullivan street, N.Y.) and Brother Ross, Saratoga Springs, and Albany (brother and sister Winder), arriving home in Philadelphia.
people: author; collecting to build a church in West Philadelphia (Rev.)

articles.headline: Married
articles.summary: Two marriages. (1) On the evening of August 28th, 1867, by Rev. R. Fauset, Mr. William [Fenn--? surname uncertain] of Queen Anne's county, Md., to Miss Mary E. Scott, of Philadelphia, Pa. (2) On August 29th, 1867, at Chester, Pa., by Rev. Wm. Murphy, Mr. Joseph Harris to Miss Emma Brown, all of Chester.

articles.headline: Died
articles.summary: In the city of Burlington, N. J., April 24th, 1867, Mrs. Susan Turner, after a short but severe illness, in the seventy-ninth year of her age. Born in Baltimore, Md., she removed early in life to Burlington, where she became one of the founders of the A. M. E. Church there; her house was the home of the first ministers; she was a zealous member of the church.
people: deceased, Burlington N.J.; a founder of Burlington A.M.E. (Mrs.)

articles.headline: Information Wanted (Louisa Steward)
articles.summary: Of my daughter, Louisa Steward, who was sold at Richmond, Va., by a man whose name is Carter, one year before the emancipation. Any information of her whereabouts will be thankfully received by her father, Daniel Steward, at Greenwich P.O., Cumberland county, N. J. Ministers please notice.
people: father (seeker), of Greenwich P.O., Cumberland Co., N.J.
daughter sought, sold at Richmond, Va.

articles.headline: A Rare Chance for a First-Class Dentist (late Dr. Crummill's office; Sarah McC. Crummill)
articles.summary: Wanted -- a first-class surgical and mechanical dentist, desiring the advantages of a long-established business, to take the office and laboratory of the late Dr. [S.] Mc. C. Crummill, who for over twenty years occupied the premises and carried on the business with a most respectable and lucrative patronage. For terms and further information apply to Sarah Mc. C. Crummill, 449 North Third Street, Philadelphia. Dateline reads approximately 'May 25 -- 1 mo' (may already be in the database; see flags).
people: advertiser, 449 North Third Street, Philadelphia; widow of the late Dr. Crummill, dentist (Mrs.)

articles.headline: Macamoose (Rev. I. R. Gates) -- depot now 813 Race Street
articles.summary: Rev. I. R. Gates' own MACAMOOSE, the Great Indian Remedy for the Blood. Price $1.00 per bottle. For sale by druggists generally and at the 'Macamoose' Depot, No. 813 Race street, Philadelphia, Pa. (The depot address 813 Race Street differs from the earlier printings at 1230 Wood St. / 1618 N. 11th -- recorded as a changed address.)
people: proprietor of Macamoose; depot No. 813 Race Street, Philadelphia (Rev.)

articles.headline: House of Application for Colored People (Mrs. Maria Butler, 1718 Sansom St.)
articles.summary: House of Application for Colored People. Mrs. Maria Butler, who has for six years opened her house for the application of colored people, male or female, who wish to obtain [employment in] any capacity in life. Any person who desires should apply to her at No. 1718 Sansom St., Philadelphia. Dated '1w' (one week -- appears new this issue).
people: proprietor, House of Application for Colored People, No. 1718 Sansom St., Philadelphia (Mrs.)

articles.headline: Freedman's Cheap Store -- Smalls & Gleaves, Beaufort, S.C.
articles.summary: STREETCAR/SMALLS WATCH ITEM (owner's watch for Robert Smalls). Freedman's Cheap Store, [street] between 4th and 5th Streets [Beaufort], wholesale and retail dealers in provisions and groceries, dry goods, trimmings, hoop skirts and notions, boots, shoes, etc. of the latest styles; highest market price paid for Sea Island cotton. Signed at head 'Cap. M. Smalls' and 'R. H. Gleaves'; footed 'Smalls & Gleaves, Beaufort, S. C.' (Beaufort, S.C. ad -- proprietors not linked as Philadelphia people, but see flags/notes: almost certainly Capt. Robert Smalls and R. H. Gleaves the former Philadelphian.)

articles.headline: Dr. William Armstrong, Drug Commission Merchant (31 North Front St.)
articles.summary: Dr. William Armstrong, Drug Commission Merchant, dealer in all kinds of foreign and domestic Roots, Herbs, and Barks, No. 31 North Front Street, Philadelphia. Advertises wanting 20,000 pounds of various roots/herbs/barks (jessamine root, dock root, snake root, etc.). Dateline 'April' -- may already be in the database; ownership (Black or white) not established.
people: proprietor, Drug Commission Merchant, No. 31 North Front Street, Philadelphia (Dr.)

articles.headline: Things in Philadelphia (editorial)
articles.summary: Last Sabbath the Holy Sacrament was administered in the Bethel church; Rev. D. Dorrell preached a very interesting discourse and a very large number partook of the Holy Eucharist. In the little church at Frankford, of which Rev. D. P. Seaton is pastor, they raised $200 -- 'Well done for Frankford!' All the churches in the city were generally well attended. Almost all the schools commenced the first Monday in this month. The Camp Meeting continued over last Sabbath, under Revs. Cornish and Hamilton. PERSONAL. Bishop A. W. Wayman was in the city last Monday and looked remarkably well.
people: preached at the Bethel church sacrament (Rev.)
pastor of the Frankford church, raised $200 (Rev.)
Bishop, in the city last Monday (Rev., Bishop)

articles.headline: Letter from Columbia, Texas
articles.author: A. Branis [VERIFY]
articles.summary: MIGRATION / A.M.E. southern mission. An A.M.E. missionary writes to let 'my many friends of Philadelphia' know of his whereabouts and missionary success in the far South-west; arrived at Columbia, Texas, Aug. 5th. Reports establishing the A.M.E. Church (to be called Campbell Chapel), with ground given by Mr. Adranta (Presbyterian) and lumber by Mr. W. G. Hill and Mr. Underwood; trustees Anthony Wilkins, Prince B. Engel, Henry Jones, James Rediv, Cornelius Hawkins; local preachers Lewis Hill and Hiram Casey; aided by Rev. Mr. Shepherd of the M.E. Church South. Signed (signature uncertain) 'A. Branis, Missionary,' Columbia, Texas, Aug. 18th, 1867. (All named persons are in Texas -- not linked.)

articles.headline: Night Schools in Philadelphia for the Fall and Winter
articles.summary: The colored citizens of Philadelphia have informed the School Controllers that they are willing to aid in the establishment of two or three night schools, so that the hundreds of colored people in the city who never had an opportunity of attending school in the day time may go at night. The Board referred the matter to the Committee on Property.

articles.headline: Information Wanted (Jeremiah and William Rhodes)
articles.summary: Information is wanted of my two sons -- Jeremiah and William Rhodes. I left them at Ellicott's Mills, Md. They belonged to Caleb Dorsey. This was before the war. Any information of their whereabouts will be thankfully received by their aged mother, Catharine Rhodes, at No. 681 Pine St., Philadelphia, Pa. Ministers please notice.
people: aged mother (seeker), No. 681 Pine St., Philadelphia
son sought, left at Ellicott's Mills, Md.
son sought, left at Ellicott's Mills, Md.

articles.headline: Married
articles.summary: In this city, on Thursday evening, July 11th, 1867, by Rev. Theodore Doughty Miller, Mr. John W. Travis to Miss Anna, daughter of Andrew Burress, Esq., all of this city. Also, in Trenton, N.J., on Wednesday, Sept. 4th, 1867, by Rev. J. Van Note, Mr. Charles Cummings to Miss Mary G. Wood, all of the above city. (A third notice -- George Quincy Jones to Miss Mary Day, both of New Haven, Conn. -- is out of town.)
people: bride, of Philadelphia, daughter of Andrew Burress
father of the bride, of Philadelphia (Esq.)

articles.headline: Notice -- African Union Church (Peter Spencer connexion)
articles.summary: The elders of the African Union Church of the Corporation and Discipline of Peter Spencer notify all whom it may concern that all churches built for and deeded to the A.U. Church, in whatever state, are claimed by those who retain the name, organization and discipline of the African Union Church. They have ordained Rev. Samuel P. Smith as minister and ruling elder, and Rev. Samuel David and Rev. William Ward as ministers and elders. States this is the first free Church of color in the United States, organized in 1813, nearly three years before Bethel, and that Rev. Samuel P. Smith was raised in it and traveled many years with Peter Spencer. Signed Rev. S. P. Smith, 1606 North St.; Rev. Samuel David; Rev. William Ward. Philadelphia, Sept., 1867.
people: ordained minister and ruling elder, African Union Church, 1606 North St., Philadelphia (Rev.)
minister and elder, African Union Church (Rev.)
minister and elder, African Union Church (Rev.)

articles.headline: Wanted -- situation to teach (Miss Martha E. Hawkins)
articles.summary: A young lady wishes a situation to teach, or as an assistant in a school, in Maryland or Virginia; no objection to a country place. With references, apply to Rev. Jas. Lynch, formerly editor of this paper. Post office address: Miss Martha E. Hawkins, Georgetown, D.C.
people: young lady seeking a teaching situation in Md./Va., Georgetown, D.C. (Miss)
reference, formerly editor of the Christian Recorder (Rev.)

articles.headline: Interesting (editorial and letter to Bishop Campbell -- steamer 'Commercial' mistreatment)
articles.author: Jas. A. Bothwell [VERIFY]
articles.summary: TRANSPORTATION-EXCLUSION ITEM. The editor introduces a letter written to Bishop Campbell, commenting that captains and conductors of steamboats and railways exclude Black passengers 'from seats to which their cashed tickets entitle them' and should learn to treat a man by his merit, not his color. The letter (Helena, Arkansas, July 25th, 1867) sympathizes with Bishop Campbell 'because of the unmanly, unchristian and Anti-American manner in which you [were] treated on the steamer Commercial.' Signed Jas. A. Bothwell. (Steamboat exclusion in Arkansas, involving a Philadelphia-Conference bishop.)
people: Bishop mistreated on the steamer 'Commercial' (Rev., Bishop)

articles.headline: A Summer Trip (travel letter -- Miss Carrie V. Still of Philadelphia at Oberlin)
articles.summary: A travel letter (left Baltimore Aug. 16 with friend James T. Bradford) to the West -- Harrisburg, Pittsburgh, Cleveland, Oberlin, Niagara, Rochester (visited Frederick Douglass). PHILADELPHIA HOOK: at Oberlin College commencement, 'Miss Carrie V. Still of Philadelphia, one of the students, seemed to be the leading spirit' in the Festival and Tableaux for the Freedmen; graduates included brother and sister John E. and Clarissa A. Patterson of Oberlin. (Cleveland Black tradesmen named in text: Freeman, Morris, Cardoso merchant tailors; Lyons; Pope; Sampson Brothers; I. F. Green; Hunterson & Alston.)
people: student at Oberlin, of Philadelphia; leading spirit of the Freedmen's Festival

articles.headline: Who Will Be Next? (editorial -- Book Concern fund)
articles.summary: The ball is started, for Philadelphia, on the $7,025. Rev. H. J. Rhodes, of Germantown, Phila., has raised, at that little place, [about $42]. On next Sunday he will lift the collection at Norristown. Let all the brethren do what they can and the required amount will be realized.
people: of Germantown, Philadelphia; raising funds toward the Book Concern debt (Rev.)

articles.headline: The True Position of the A.M.E. Church of America (editorial)
articles.summary: A long editorial by the Editor (Weaver) stating the position of the African Methodist Episcopal Church: its Methodist faith and government; itinerancy; prayer-, class- and love-feast meetings; the history of its separation from the M.E. Church over slavery and prejudice at the Lord's Table; that 'God put into the heart of our Richard Allen... to make a grand reform,' the body being firmly organized in 1816 with 'African' inserted in the title; its bishops, elders and preachers; perfect equality without distinction of color; and its willingness to reunite with the M.E. Church North on terms of full equality.
people: A.M.E. founder cited as making the 'grand reform'; organized 1816 (historical)

articles.headline: Bishop Campbell and the M.E. Church Controversy
articles.summary: For the Christian Recorder. Philadelphia, Sept. 16, 1867. On the controversy between some ministers of the M.E. Church and the A.M.E. Church in the Mississippi Valley and Northwest; the presiding Bishop, J. P. Campbell, had been denounced over references to his administration and alleged favoritism to the M.E. Church South. Owing to yellow fever in his field, Campbell came to Philadelphia and, to vindicate himself, the Bishop, Rev. E. Weaver, Rev. John M. Brown, Rev. S. H. Williams and other friends went to the M.E. Preachers' Meeting; Bishop Campbell spoke at length denying he charged the M.E. Church with stealing church property, and recounting a Nashville church bought over the heads of the A.M.E. members. Rev. John W. Brown (imprisoned at New Orleans) was present. M.E. ministers named in text: Dr. Newman (New Orleans Advocate), Brakeman, Knight, Welch, and Mr. Walsh.
people: Bishop vindicating himself at the Philadelphia Preachers' Meeting (Rev., Bishop)
of the Bishop's party at the meeting (Rev.)
of the Bishop's party at the meeting (Rev.)
of the Bishop's party at the meeting (Rev.)
present; had been imprisoned at New Orleans (Rev.)

articles.headline: Married (Norristown)
articles.summary: At Norristown, Pa., Sept. 18, 1867, by the Rev. Jeremiah Young, Mr. Nathaniel L. Snyder of Virginia, to Miss Ella L. Curry, of Chester, Pa.

articles.headline: Things in Philadelphia (editorial)
articles.summary: On last Sabbath morning we attended Bethel church and heard Bishop Campbell, D.D., preach -- one of the ablest sermons on the subject we have ever listened to; in connection he gave an account of his travels in the South; at the conclusion they gave him nearly forty dollars. At night we attended the Presbyterian church, of which Rev. John B. Reeves is pastor, and heard Mr. Cardozo discourse, giving a very fine account of his work in Charleston, South Carolina, and the educational success there, referring especially to that of Rev. R. H. Cain.
people: Bishop, preached at Bethel church (Rev., Bishop)
pastor of the (First African) Presbyterian church, Philadelphia (Rev.)

articles.headline: Matrimonial (John Ballard and Mary Elizabeth Gibbs)
articles.summary: We had the pleasure of uniting Mr. John Ballard and Miss Mary Elizabeth Gibbs in the bonds of holy wedlock, on the 21st inst. Both of Philadelphia. The ceremony took place at our residence, No. 619 Pine street, in this city.
people: officiating (editor, at his residence 619 Pine St.) (Rev.)

articles.headline: Married
articles.summary: On the 22d of September, 1867, by the Rev. James Frisby, Mr. Wm. Moore, of Baltimore, Md., to Miss Mary Barfield, of Philadelphia, Pa. Also, Sept. 22d, 1867, by the Rev. Henry Davis (New York), Mr. Wm. C. Miller to Miss Mary A. Todd, formerly of Philadelphia. (Two further New York marriages by Rev. Henry Davis -- Richard M. Thompson to Henrietta Davis, and Wm. H. Miller to Henrietta Adams -- are out of town.)
people: bride, formerly of Philadelphia (married in New York, Sept. 22, 1867)

articles.headline: Died (Henry Wilson)
articles.summary: Died, on the 25th instant, Mr. Henry Wilson, an old and much esteemed resident of this city (in Pine street, above Sixth), aged [--] years. He leaves a kind and affectionate wife and other friends. He was, we believe, a member of Bethel church; had been lingering a long time under a paralytic stroke.
people: deceased, old resident of Philadelphia (Pine St. above Sixth); member of Bethel church (Mr.)

articles.headline: Information Wanted (James Tillman)
articles.summary: Information wanted of my two brothers, Jerry James and Charles Moore, and of my sister, Lydia Bell. They were sold from the Wm. Corkelle(?) estate into George[s] Co., Md. Any information concerning their whereabouts will be thankfully received by their brother, James Tillman. Please address James Tillman, Bridgewater Post Office, Bucks Co., Pa.
people: brother (seeker), Bridgewater P.O., Bucks Co., Pa.

articles.headline: Letter from Lincoln University (Hosanna, Chester Co., Pa.)
articles.summary: A Lincoln University (Oxford, Chester Co., Pa.) student's vacation letter: he taught a school at the Hosanna Methodist Church neighborhood (July 1 - Sept.), then a picnic for the pupils and parents in the woods, with addresses by Messrs. Reece, H. Chrestfield(?), Wm. Miller, and the writer, all students of the University. (Names are Lincoln University students; recorded in text.)

events.name: The Philadelphia Conference -- Union Camp Meeting at Media, Pennsylvania
events.description: Report of the Philadelphia Conference Union Camp Meeting at Media, Pa., held the preceding Sabbath (about Sept. 1, 1867); eight or nine thousand persons present. Services: at half-past 6 o'clock Rev. Jacob Mitchell; at half-past 10 o'clock Rev. Wm. Moore; at 3 o'clock Bishop A. W. Wayman (subject 'Eternity,' one of his most powerful sermons); at night Rev. J. B. Hamilton (many came forward to be prayed for and were converted). Editor criticizes the selling of fruit on the Lord's day.
attendees: preached at half-past 10 (Rev.) [identity: one of several Wm. Moores -- as printed]

events.name: Book Committee meeting (A.M.E. Book Concern)
events.description: Notice: The Book Committee will please meet at the Book Rooms on Monday, Sept. 9, at half-past nine o'clock, A.M. No names printed.

events.location: Pennsylvania, Delaware, New Jersey, Maryland, Virginia
events.description: Special Notice of Bishop Wayman's appointments: Sun. Sept. 8 Frankford, Pa.; Thu. Sept. 12 Chester, Pa.; Sun. Sept. 15 ordination, Lancaster, Pa.; Tue. Sept. 22 dedication, Laurel, Del.; Mon. night Sept. 23 Sanford(?), Del.; Tue. night Sept. 24 Union Church, Del.; Wed. night Sept. 25 Lock Woods, Del.; Thu. night Sept. 26 Grime's Chapel, Del.; Sun. events.name: A.M.E. Book Concern debt assessment on the Annual Conferences ($7,025)
events.description: Special Notice to the members of the Baltimore, Philadelphia, New York, Virginia, South Carolina, Georgia and Florida Annual Conferences. The Philadelphia Conference recommended that $7,025 be raised to relieve the Book Concern debt, proportioned by the Committee of Book Concern: Baltimore Conference ~$1000, Philadelphia $1000, New York $700, Virginia $100, South Carolina $500, Georgia $200, Florida $200. Funds to be raised by the first of October and sent to Rev. E. Weaver, No. 631 Pine street, Philadelphia, or Box 2953. Signed A. W. Wayman.
attendees: Bishop who signed the assessment (Rev., Bishop)
editor/publisher, to receive funds, 631 Pine St. (Rev.)

events.name: Harvest Home and Festival for the Chester A.M.E. Church
events.description: A Harvest Home and Festival at National Hall, Chester, Pa., on Thursday, September 12th, for the benefit of the A.M.E. church at Chester. Exercises: singing and addresses by Bishop Wayman, Revs. E. Weaver, J. Hamilton, D. P. Seaton, Jos. H. Smith, Stephen Smith, and others. Dinner at 1 o'clock (50 cents); festival in the evening (admission 20 cents). Tickets at the office of the Christian Recorder, 631 Pine Street, Phila. Philadelphians can reach Chester via the Baltimore Railroad or the steamer Ariel (Chestnut street wharf 9.45 A.M. and 3.45 P.M.). Jeremiah Young, Pastor.
attendees: pastor of the Chester A.M.E. church (Rev.)

events.name: Macedonia A.M.E. Church, Camden, N.J. -- monthly communion
events.description: Notice: The monthly communion at Macedonia, Sunday, 8th inst., at 3 o'clock, P.M.; the brethren and sisters of sister churches are invited. J. S. Hamilton, Pastor, Camden, N.J., Sept. 7.

events.name: Quarterly Conference appointments (Elder H. Harris in charge)
events.location: Rockingham Mountain, New Hope, Stroudsburg, Attleborough (Pa.)
events.description: Notice: Quarterly Conference at Rockingham Mountain on the 14th and 15th of September; 21st and 22d at New Hope; 28th and 29th at Stroudsburg; October 5th and 6th at Attleborough, Pa. Signed H. Harris(?), Elder in charge.

events.name: Burlington, N.J. Sabbath-school Picnic and Temperance Meeting
events.description: Notice: A grand Sabbath-school Picnic at Burlington, N.J., on the 12th of September, 1867, in the grove; a Temperance Meeting the same evening in the church; refreshments of all kinds. Jacob Mitchell, Pastor.

events.name: Macedonia A.M.E. Church, Camden, N.J. -- Quarterly Meeting
events.description: Quarterly Meeting at Macedonia, Sunday, September 22d. Love-feast in the morning at 8 1/2 o'clock. Preaching: at 11 o'clock Rev. Wm. Moore; at 3 o'clock Rev. D. Dorrell; at 8 o'clock Rev. G. E. Boyer. J. B. Hamilton, Pastor. Camden, N.J., September 10, 1867.

events.name: Grand Concert at the Cherry Street Baptist Church
events.description: On the 26th inst. a grand concert will be given at the Cherry Street Baptist church, of which Rev. Theodore D. Miller is the accredited pastor. events.name: A Statement -- Committee of the Union Camp Meeting of the Philadelphia District (Media)
events.description: The Committee of the Union Camp Meeting of the Philadelphia District thank the people of Philadelphia and of the vicinity of Media. The meeting ran August 24 to September 8, 1867, embracing one Sabbath, notable for Bishop Wayman's sermon on 'Eternity'; not less than 15,000 people on the ground and no disorder. Committee: Rev. D. Dorrell, Rev. William Moore, Rev. G. E. Boyer, Rev. D. P. Seaton, Rev. H. J. Rhodes, Rev. J. B. Hamilton, Rev. Jacob Mitchell, Rev. J. Young, Rev. W. Williams.

events.name: Bishop Campbell to preach at Bethel and Union churches

events.description: Notice: Bishop Campbell will preach at Bethel Church, South Sixth street, below Pine, at 10 o'clock A.M., and Union church, Coates Street, below Fifth, at 7 1/2 P.M., next Sabbath, Sept. 22d, 1867.
attendees: Bishop, preaching at Bethel and Union (Rev., Bishop)

events.name: Missionary meeting addressed by Rev. John M. Brown at Wesley church
events.description: Personal: Rev. John M. Brown addressed a missionary meeting, on the 19th instant, at Wesley church. There was not a very large attendance, but those present did what they could for the cause of missions.

events.name: Reception of Gen. Phil. Sheridan in Philadelphia (procession)
events.location: Baltimore & Philadelphia Depot to the Continental Hotel (via Arch and Twelfth streets), Philadelphia
events.description: General Sheridan arrived at the Baltimore and Philadelphia Depot on Wednesday evening, Sept. 25; the largest crowd ever seen in Philadelphia assembled from the depot to Arch street and along Twelfth to the Continental Hotel. Portions of the grand army of the Potomac, white and colored, paraded, and the fire companies turned out. The General rode in an open barouche, accompanied by Mayor McMichael. (Parade with colored troops; no Black individuals named.)

events.name: Laying of the corner-stone of the A.M.E. Church, Carlisle, Pa.
events.description: Procession formed at 2 o'clock on Centre Square. Order of procession: Bishop Wayman; Rev. Amos Wilson, pastor; ministers of the different denominations; the Douglass Equal Rights League of Carlisle; a detachment of colored soldiers from the Barracks; Freemasons from Harrisburg and other places; led by a drum corps. Bishop Wayman gave out the hymn and delivered the address; prayer by Rev. Wm. H. Keith (white) of the M.E. Church. Articles deposited in the corner-stone: the Bible, Discipline, Hymn Book, Apostles' Creed, Minutes of the Baltimore Conference, Christian Recorder dated Aug. 17, 1867, and names of the President, Governor of Pennsylvania, minister in charge, Trustees and Building Committee. The minister's call was for $200.
attendees: Bishop, laid the corner-stone and gave the address (Rev., Bishop)

events.name: Thanks for a festival of the Lancaster City, Pa. charge
events.description: A card of thanks (to the Editor): the minister thanks the young ladies and gentlemen of his charge in Lancaster City, Pa., and especially the young ladies of the committee, who presented him with $11.40, the proceeds of a festival held on the 4th of September, 1867. Committee: Misses Catharine Johnson, Anna Moore, Mary Morris, and Mrs. Harriet West. James V. Pierce, Minister.
attendees: minister of the Lancaster City, Pa. charge (Rev.)
